page: Microsoft Azure F4ams_v7 is a memory-intensive virtual machine belonging to the Famsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated physical cores and 4 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor with an x86_64 architecture. The CPU operates at a high base clock speed of 4.5 GHz and is equipped with 32 MB of L3 cache. It includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 (including AVX512_VNNI and AVX512_BF16) and cryptography acceleration via AES and SHA_NI.

The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage, but it is capable of utilizing Premium Storage. There are no complimentary public IPv4 addresses bundled with this server type, and it does not feature any GPU accelerators.

In benchmark evaluations, the F4ams_v7 exhibits top-tier single-core performance, as evidenced by its stress-ng single-core CPU score of 3658.18 and a Geekbench single-core score of 2447.0. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also rank in the top 10%. Multi-core operations, memory bandwidth (uncached read at 53.49 GB/sec and write at 34.49 GB/sec), and database operations perform in the average tier. However, prompt processing for medium-sized LLM models is relatively weak, though text generation for smaller models remains highly efficient.

Given its high memory density relative to the 4 dedicated vCPUs, this server offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring substantial memory footprints without needing massive parallel compute scaling. It is well-suited for memory-intensive applications, database operations, text processing, and single-threaded data compression tasks.
